title: Canonical finite coefficient comparison data on both small sites
statement: For finite coefficient rings A and B and a homomorphism phi, use the actual ordinary etale and pro-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Scalar extension, tensor and internal Hom are the published derived functors [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Direct comparison is the inverse-image/direct-image counit mate; closed comparison is the transpose of the inverse direct comparison and the extended closed counit [lem-exc-closed-ambient, lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. The dualizing object is exceptional inverse image of the regular coefficient unit, and its scalar arrow is the corresponding compact-support counit mate followed by the unit comparison [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, def-per-exceptional-coefficient-maps]. The internal-Hom arrow is the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation through a normalized balanced tensorator. Verdier comparison is internal-Hom comparison followed by the dualizing arrow. All potentially undefined inverses are extended by zero away from their isomorphism domain. For the finite stages [def-coef-finite-coefficient-stages], Calculus packages those maps, normalized tensorators and Koszul symmetries, constructible finite-Tor preservation, the five isomorphism assertions, evaluation and double-dual identities, naturality, units and composition. Normalized identifies the ordinary arrows with their counit definitions and specifies the etale/pro-etale site squares, including the site unit and counit. DirectGeometry, HomGeometry, ClosedGeometry, ExceptionalGeometry and their four pro-etale versions are the explicit coefficient/geometric squares under scheme isomorphisms. These are definitions and fields of data; no assertion that a Calculus exists is made here.
